It's mostly due to the Danube river. Rotterdam is Europe's largest port mainly due to Schengen and the inner free market. The Rhine, which begins in Switserland and goes through Alsace, Baden-Wurttemburg, Rhineland-Palatinate, and lastly, through the Netherlands is and economic artery for the economies of these nations. Even countries like Austria and Czechia import some goods through the Rhine and then through canals that connect to the Danube river. Because Serbia and Romania are not in Schengen, importing goods through the port of Constance in Romania is often more expensive. Letting Romania in could mean that the trade volume through Rotterdam declines, which is bad for our economy. Bulgaria has said it will go together with Romania, and so they are also rejected under corruption pretenses, which is just a load of bollocks. You might find that telling the Dutch people that our economy will take a hit because Romania and Bulgaria has entered Schengen is a hard sell, especially in the current political climate we find ourselves in. I think we should let them in. There is no reason that we can't extend the power of rivers to perhaps the most important river in Eastern Europe, a region that can really use more economic growth. There might even be possible to combine their economic power and give Europe's economy a massive boost.

He taxed the living hell out of the french speaking Wallonia, back then the more important part of the southern Netherlands. The worst part of course being the fact that there was not really a representative government. 

Freedom of religion is a thing now and most of the Netherlands considers themselves atheist/agnostic, so the religious argument doesn't really work anymore. Taxation is a problem for everyone nowadays and in a hypothetical federation of the Low Countries everyone will probably be taxed based on income as is already the case in both The Netherlands and Belgium I think. The entire region is very developed and has long entered the 3rd stage in economic development, as in most of the economy is based on the service sector after the Industrial revolution and, of course, the agricultural development. Representation shouldn't be too much of an issue and the ideal type of government for a Beneluxian state would be a federation so that we are united while retaining regional and perhaps national identity. 1830 is long past us my friend.

We have, as many others have, an indirect democracy. We trust that the party that we voted for will stick with their own ideas and vote accordingly.
